change_summary: The paper has been withdrawn. Its text was replaced by a statement saying the indoor temperature records were processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the results cannot be relied on. This affects every finding that rests on those records, such as the reported 2.1 °C lower daily peak indoor temperature and 41% fewer hours above 28 °C in green-roofed flats. The withdrawal happened before final publication.
evaluation: Your draft takes the 2.1 °C indoor cooling effect from Okafor et al. [14] and uses it as the key green-roof parameter in Section 2.2. The Discussion and Conclusions rest on it too. The paper has been withdrawn because its indoor temperature records were processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so that value is no longer reliable. This reaches the Results (about half of person-hours avoided), the comparison with reflective coatings, and the programme recommendation. The impact is high.
recommendation: The Okafor et al. paper was withdrawn because its indoor temperature records used an incorrect sensor calibration, and your model takes its 2.1 °C green-roof parameter from it. Raise this with your co-authors or supervisor, replace the parameter, rerun the results, and remove or rewrite the Discussion claims that rest on it.

alerts.what_changed: The paper's own DOI now carries a withdrawal statement in place of the article. The editor was told the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the results cannot be relied on. The full text and PDF were replaced by this statement.
alerts.reason: The content was withdrawn and the notice says the reported results cannot be relied on because of a data-processing error. This covers all findings, including the 2.1 °C lower peak indoor temperature.
